chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who killed two men intentionally, and both had heirs. Then the heirs of one of them pardoned, while the others refused. He said: He said, “Those who did not pardon may kill him, and if they prefer to take the blood-money, they may take it.”

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: So I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Two men killed one man intentionally, and he has two heirs, then one of the two heirs pardoned. He said: He said, “When some of the heirs pardon, killing is averted from the two of them, and from the blood-money there is deducted from them according to the share of the one who pardoned, and they shall pay the remainder from their wealth to those who did not pardon.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ: legal heirs entitled to claim retaliation or blood-money
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money paid as financial compensation for killing
key_terms.حِصَّةِ: share or legal portion attributed to an heir
key_terms.دُرِئَ: was averted or removed; here, the death penalty is lifted
key_terms.عَفَا: pardoned; waived the right of retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if some heirs pardon in a case of intentional murder while others do not?
ai.summary: This hadith explains legal rulings concerning intentional killing when multiple heirs differ over pardon and retaliation. It establishes that non-pardoning heirs may demand qisas or accept diyah, and that when some heirs pardon in a case involving multiple killers, the death penalty is removed and the remaining diyah is paid in proportion to the shares of those who did not pardon.
